subject_session: sub-LA11/ses-1 (primary); also LA3, LA8, LA9, LA12

headline_stat.name: tone-responsive fraction / median onset latency / GLM held-out PSTH r

justification.dataset: Pure-tone dataset 000986 cannot isolate a genuine spectrotemporal receptive field, which the rubric explicitly notes requires spectrotemporally rich (ripple/natural) stimuli, so the requested phenomenon is only marginally present.
justification.handling: Real data streamed correctly with proper tone-onset alignment, but no unit quality filtering is applied and inclusion rests only on a peak z-score criterion.
justification.analysis: The per-frequency PSTH (an FRA) is computed correctly and cross-checked with a Poisson GLM, though the peak-z responsiveness test is somewhat anticonservative and no shuffle null is used.
justification.correctness: Reported values (82% responsive, 27 ms latency, r=0.76/0.86) reproduce from the committed code and are internally consistent and physically possible.
justification.figures: Figures are clean, well-labeled with units and sample sizes, use representative (strongest-responding) examples, and clearly show the computed tone-tuning effect.
justification.honesty: Mild-to-moderate overstatement: a pure-tone FRA is presented as a bona-fide STRF ('the canonical mean auditory-cortex STRF,' 'robust, general property') with zero stated limitations, but numbers are real and no capping act is cleanly triggered.
justification.verdict: The chosen pure-tone data cannot demonstrate the requested spectrotemporal receptive field, and the central STRF conclusion is presented as clean without any caveat, so an expert would send it back.
